questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I studied at the University of Sydney (USYD) during my final semester of Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy. My previous travels to Australia during my gap year between High School and University left an immense impact on me and made me safe assured in choosing USYD as my top priority over the other options: Dublin University, Bath University, and Zürich University. 

Career opportunities were also an important factor in my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall a great study experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international study coordinators at USYD were extremely helpful - big thanks to them! However, the digital platforms, particularly the timetable system, could be more improved by making it more user-friendly and compliant.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recived help with setting up my time table to include my preferred units of study as well as finding the most suitable timeslots.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very good!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I were staying at the Queen Mary Building (QMB) in Camperdown

Other options include Abercrombie Student Accommodation, Darlington House, The Regiment, UniLodge Kensington, and Scape

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Large shared kitchen area (20-30 stoves)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living in campus housing is a great way to meet other international students from around the world and to enjoy the benefits of being close to the university. Sydney is a massive city, and living in popular areas like Bondi Beach and Kings Cross can easily mean up to 40 minutes transport each way. Be mindfull of that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super nice facilities!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Converting Australian Credit Points (CP) to the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS) was challanging, and it wasn't easy to find the relevant units of study online. There were so many options to choose from!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1) Students receive a USYD student ID number, which is required to create their University of Sydney application account online.
2) The application must include personal details such as full name, address, academic background, and other relevant information.
3) Applicants must apply for an approved visa—specifically, the Student Visa (subclass 500)—through the Australian Government’s Department of Home Affairs.
4) Proof of sufficient English proficiency is required, such as a high school diploma (if applicable) or results from an approved English test like the TOEFL iBT.
5) Applicants must also obtain Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), a mandatory health insurance for international students in Australia.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Suppor during the application process was limited, so I relied on advice from students who had previously gone through it to help guide me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My application was very successful, and I was able to enroll in all the classes I had hoped for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your best to complete the application on your own, and don’t hesitate to seek help if anything is unclear

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were generally on the same academic level as UCPH. However, the workload, measured in hours spent on studying, were noticable lighter at USYD.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Significantly less time was spent on laboratory work and report writing at USYD compared to UCPH. Aside from that, most aspects of the coursework were quite similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EDUH4052	Learning in Outdoor Education, PCOL3012 Drug Design and Development, and PHAR4815	Research Methods

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: EDUH4052 Learning in Outdoor Education: This unit offers a unique opportunity to explore the diverse Australian landscapes in New South Wales alongside other international students. Designed specifically for exchange students, the course provides a great chance to connect with fellow participants while engaging in outdoor learning experiences.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There’s a wide range of societies and social clubs - too many to count! No matter your interests, there’s something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Surf Society: A fun and energetic group known for great vibes both in the water and at their legendary parties. They are known for their yearly surfcamp/party!
Bouldering Society: A lively and active club that explores a variety of climbing gyms and bouldering centers across Sydney.
Unofficial Run Club x Fishbowl Sydney: One of Sydney’s best run clubs, offering scenic runs and a strong community vibe—conveniently based near Bondi Junction.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go travelling! Australia is a great country to travel in. It's almost to big.

I would personally reccomend the following:
Sydney:
- ALL the beaches (Manly, Shelly, Coogee, Bronte, Bondi, etc.) 
- Blue Mountains 
- Glebe or Paddington markets (Saturday)
- Taronga Zoo
- Watching Aussie Footy (Australian Football)

Melbourne:
- Great Ocean Road and The 12 Apostels
- Philip Island and Pingvin parade
- Shopping and café tours

Other places to go...
- Byron Bay
- Fraiser Island
- Magnetic Island
- Whitsundays Islands
- Great Barrier Reef (Cairns)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Expect to spend about a month settling in and adjusting to the new environment.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to join as many events as possible at the beginning of the semester - there is many to choose from, and it’s a great way to meet new people. With so many students at USYD, it can feel overwhelming, so focus on finding a smaller group of friends you really connect with. Spend time together doing simple things like cooking, going on trips, or watching sports and movies. It makes the experience much more enjoyable and grounded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Studying at USYD requires a high level of independence. You need to manage your time effectively to stay on top of your coursework and fully participate in classes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fun and laid-back Australian lifestyle is something special:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Make an effort to meet as many new people as you can
2) Stay open-minded and embrace the diversity of different cultural backgrounds
3) Be inclusive and kind - everyone deserves to feel welcome when being on exchange far from home

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Share your knowledge across borders and support both international and domestic students with academically challenging tasks. At UCPH, we have a strong foundation in pharmaceutical sciences and it's worth sharing!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning more about my field of study (Pharmacy), while learning other culturally different backgrounds

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being independent and establish a network of new friends far from Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your stay at USYD!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
